summary.title: Generation Models Know Space: Unleashing Implicit 3D Priors for Scene Understanding

details: MLLMs are 'spatially blind': discriminative visual encoders trained with sparse token-level supervision lack geometric/metric structure.
Existing remedies need explicit 3D input (point clouds/depth) or geometric scaffolding (BEV reconstruction, 3D-teacher distillation), which is annotation-hungry and hard to scale.
VEGA-3D: repurposes a frozen pretrained video diffusion model as a 'Latent World Simulator' that supplies label-free implicit 3D priors to an MLLM visual stream.

Priors are activated by re-noising the clean VAE latent along the model's flow-matching path to an intermediate timestep and reading out an intermediate DiT layer's features with an empty text prompt (no generation, no denoising rollout).
A token-level adaptive gated fusion convexly mixes generative and semantic tokens with a per-token sigmoid gate, acting as a semantic-geometric arbitrator.
Diagnostic tool motivating the design: a multi-view correspondence score measuring cosine similarity of features of the same voxel across views (using GT depth/pose only for analysis).
3D scene understanding: Video-3D LLM baseline + Wan2.1-T2V 1.3B generative branch; trained multi-task on ScanRefer, Multi3DRefer, Scan2Cap, ScanQA, SQA3D (ScanNet scenes).
Spatial reasoning: Qwen2.5VL-7B baseline finetuned on VG-LLM's S1 mixture (SPAR-7M + LLaVA-Hound split), evaluated on VSI-Bench.
Embodied: OpenVLA-OFT on LIBERO four suites (visual stream only augmented, policy/LLM unchanged); plus real Agilex Piper arm 'Click Bell' task under RoboTwin protocol.
32 uniformly sampled frames per scan; features from 20th DiT block at flow-matching timestep k=300 (K=1000), empty text prompt; adaptive average pooling to 14x14=196 tokens per frame.
Voxel size 0.1 m for correspondence score; 8x H100, Adam, batch 128, LR 1e-5 (LLM) / 2e-6 (visual backbone).
Per-scene feature caching to amortize inference overhead.
Generative encoders swapped in: Wan2.1-T2V, Wan2.1-VACE (DiT) vs. Stable Video Diffusion, SD 2.1, Vmem, SEVA (UNet), plus raw VAE latents.
Discriminative/3D encoders as alternative priors: DINOv3-Large, V-JEPA v2, VGGT.
Normalized Overall Score (NOS) computed per group (min-max over 9 metrics, baseline included) and correlated with correspondence score.
Fusion variants: generative-only, Add, channel concat+MLP, sequence concat, 1/3-layer cross-attention, channel-level gating vs. token-level adaptive gating.
Diffusion timestep sweep k=0..1000 (also for SEVA and Vmem) and DiT layer sweep (blocks 10,12,15,20,25,28).

key_findings.finding: Label-free priors from a frozen video generator match or beat methods using explicit 3D/geometric supervision on 3D scene understanding.
key_findings.evidence: On top of Video-3D LLM, VEGA-3D raises ScanRefer Acc@0.5 from 51.7 to 56.2, Multi3DRefer F1@0.5 52.7 to 55.1, ScanQA CIDEr 102.1 to 106.3, SQA3D EM 58.6 to 61.3, achieving the best average rank (2.2) over 20+ specialists/generalists including 3DRS (2.7) and BEV-supervised Ross3D (2.6), and leading on all grounding metrics.

key_findings.finding: Multi-view feature correspondence is a strong predictor of downstream 3D understanding, and DiT-based video generators dominate UNet-based ones on this axis.
key_findings.evidence: Correspondence score correlates positively with the Normalized Overall Score across backbones; Wan2.1-VACE/T2V reach ~97% correspondence and the highest generative-group NOS (89.3/82.4), whereas SVD and SD2.1 score 17.9/23.8 correspondence and 52.1/70.6 NOS.

key_findings.finding: The most useful spatial signal lies at intermediate denoising noise levels and intermediate network depth, not in clean latents or final layers.
key_findings.evidence: Timestep sweep peaks at k=300 (ScanRefer Acc@0.25 63.2) versus 62.4 at k=0 and 61.4 at k=1000; layer sweep peaks at block 20 (63.2) versus 62.3 at block 10 and 61.4 at block 28; SEVA and Vmem show a similar mid-timestep preference.

key_findings.finding: Generative priors are complementary to semantic features and require adaptive token-level gating rather than fixed fusion.
key_findings.evidence: Using generative features alone collapses performance (Scan2Cap CIDEr 25.2, ScanQA CIDEr 74.0 vs. baseline 83.8/102.1); adaptive gated fusion beats Add, sequence concat, cross-attention (Scan2Cap CIDEr 47.8-48.8) and channel-level gating, e.g. ScanRefer Acc@0.25 63.2 vs. 61.5 (Add) and 61.8 (channel gating).

key_findings.finding: The prior transfers to embodied control without any action-conditioned or 3D training.
key_findings.evidence: On LIBERO, adding the frozen generative branch to OpenVLA-OFT raises average success 97.0 to 97.3 with gains on Object (98.3 to 99.4) and Long (94.4 to 95.2); on real Agilex Piper Click Bell, success rises from 40% (8/20) to 55% (11/20). On VSI-Bench, Qwen2.5VL-7B improves 48.9 to 50.5 average.
